reports.title: Índice de Precios al Consumidor (IPC) / Consumer Price Index
reports.description: Monthly consumer price index measuring changes in the prices of a representative basket of goods and services of urban households. Geographic coverage: regional capitals and conurbations. Base currently 2023=100; next base change planned for 2028 after the 10th EPF.
reports._notes: Flagship price statistic. Published on the 8th of each month (or previous business day). Directly used by the Banco Central de Chile for inflation monitoring and for the UF/UTM adjustment mechanisms. July 2026 monthly variation 0.1%.

reports.title: Encuesta Nacional de Empleo (ENE) / National Employment Survey
reports.description: Continuous household survey producing the official labour-market indicators: employment, unemployment, labour force participation, informal employment, and related rates. Published as moving quarters.
reports._notes: Core labour survey. April–June 2026: national unemployment rate 9.4%; informal employment rate 27.0%. Microdata and detailed tables released regularly. Experimental dimensions (skill mismatch, etc.) recently added.

reports.title: Cuentas Nacionales / National Accounts of Chile
reports.publisher: Banco Central de Chile (with INE source data)
reports.description: Full system of national accounts producing GDP by production, expenditure and income, institutional sector accounts and related aggregates. Compiled by the Central Bank; many volume and price inputs from INE.
reports._notes: In Chile the central bank is the primary compiler of the national accounts, using extensive INE source statistics. Quarterly GDP and annual institutional accounts are the headline products.

reports.title: Índice de Producción Industrial (IPI) / Industrial Production Index
reports.description: Monthly volume index of industrial production (manufacturing, mining, electricity/gas/water). Principal short-term activity indicator for the industrial sector.
reports._notes: Core short-term industrial indicator. May 2026: +1.6% year-on-year. Complements the broader activity measures produced by the Central Bank.

reports.title: Medición de la pobreza por ingresos / Income poverty measurement
reports.publisher: Ministerio de Desarrollo Social y Familia + INE + CEPAL technical support
reports.description: Official income-poverty measurement based on a basic food basket and non-food component, updated with methodological revisions (most recent major update process 2025). Uses household survey income data and IPC for price updating.
reports._notes: Headline social indicator. Methodology recently reviewed with CEPAL, INE and MDSF participation. Canasta Básica de Alimentos constructed from the EPF and updated with IPC food prices.

reports.title: Encuesta de Presupuestos Familiares (EPF) / Family Budget Survey
reports.description: Periodic household expenditure survey that supplies the weights and basket for the CPI and is a key input into the poverty-line construction. 10th round scheduled 2026–2027 for the 2028 CPI base change.
reports._notes: Structural survey underpinning both the CPI and the poverty methodology. Next round (10ª EPF) begins collection September 2026 and will drive the 2028=100 CPI base.

reports.title: Censo de Población y Vivienda / Population and Housing Census
reports.description: Decennial population and housing census. Provides the demographic baseline and sampling frames for household surveys. Latest major census 2017; next cycle in preparation.
reports._notes: Foundational demographic product. Population projections and survey designs continuously reference the census baseline.

reports.title: Indicador de Actividad Económica Regional (INACER)
reports.description: Regional economic activity indicator produced by INE for the regions of Chile. Provides a geographic disaggregation of short-term activity.
reports._notes: Regional counterpart to the national activity measures. Useful for the later regional/metro hierarchy fill.
reports._domains_note: Tagged general-statistics (promoted into the Domain union 2026-08-18). This is a general multi-domain statistical compendium — a state/district yearbook or abstract — and its only original tag was a geographic or 'comprehensive' pseudo-tag that the 2026-08-18 domain pass dropped. Dropping 'comprehensive' was right for batch-meta nodes and wrong here: for a yearbook, 'covers everything' is a fact about the content. Asserting the individual domains it covers would be inventing them.

reports.title: Índice de Producción Minera (IPMin)
reports.description: Monthly volume index of mining production (metallic, non-metallic, energy resources). Component of the broader IPI. Critical for a mining-intensive economy.
reports._notes: Flagship mining volume indicator. June 2026: +6.0% year-on-year. Lithium carbonate and metallic mining frequently drive the swings. Direct input into national accounts and external-sector analysis.

reports.title: Índice de Producción Manufacturera (IPMan)
reports.description: Monthly volume index of manufacturing production. Component of the IPI.
reports._notes: Manufacturing counterpart to the mining index. June 2026: −3.2% year-on-year in one recent release window. Food processing and other divisions regularly detailed.

reports.title: Índice de Producción de Electricidad, Gas y Agua (IPEGA)
reports.description: Monthly volume index of electricity, gas and water production/distribution. Component of the IPI.
reports._notes: Utilities component of industrial production. Completes the three-pillar IPI structure (mining, manufacturing, EGA).

reports.title: Índice de Actividad del Comercio (IAC)
reports.description: Monthly index of commercial activity (wholesale, retail, automotive). Published at constant prices with electronic-commerce and supermarket sub-indices.
reports._notes: Principal short-term commerce indicator. Recent releases have shown solid retail and automotive contributions; electronic-commerce sub-index frequently grows double-digit.

reports.title: IMACEC — Indicador Mensual de Actividad Económica
reports.description: Monthly estimator of economic activity compiled by the Central Bank. Primary high-frequency GDP proxy, drawing on INE volume indicators and other sources.
reports._notes: Chilean counterpart to Argentina’s EMAE. Central Bank product that integrates the INE industrial, commerce and other monthly series into a single activity measure.

reports.title: Balanza de Pagos y Posición de Inversión Internacional
reports.description: Quarterly balance of payments and international investment position. Covers current account, capital/financial account, and the stock of external assets and liabilities.
reports._notes: Core external-accounts product. Q1 2026: current-account surplus of USD 1.9 bn (1.9% of GDP). Annual yearbook and detailed quarterly releases available.

reports.title: Estadísticas de Comercio Exterior / Merchandise Trade
reports.publisher: Banco Central de Chile / Aduanas (with INE support)
reports.description: Monthly and quarterly statistics of exports and imports of goods, including copper and other mining products, by partner and by product.
reports._notes: Trade data feed both the balance of payments and the national accounts. Copper remains the dominant single export; lithium and other non-metallic minerals are rising.

reports.title: Base monetaria y agregados monetarios
reports.description: Regular statistics of the monetary base and broader monetary aggregates (M1, M2, etc.) published by the Central Bank.
reports._notes: Core monetary statistics. Published in the Central Bank’s statistical bulletins and database with clear definitions of the aggregates.

reports.title: Índices Nominales de Remuneraciones y de Costos Laborales
reports.description: Monthly indices of nominal wages and labour costs. Complement the ENE employment statistics with a price-of-labour measure.
reports._notes: Wage and labour-cost counterpart to the employment survey. June 2026: nominal remunerations +7.7% year-on-year; labour costs +8.4%.

reports.title: Encuesta de Caracterización Socioeconómica Nacional (CASEN)
reports.publisher: Ministerio de Desarrollo Social y Familia (with INE methodological support)
reports.description: Periodic multi-purpose household survey that is the primary source for multidimensional and income poverty estimates, living conditions, and social-programme targeting.
reports._notes: Key social survey. Complements the income-poverty methodology that uses EPF and IPC. Provides the broader living-conditions picture used in policy evaluation.

reports.title: Región Metropolitana de Santiago (RMS) — core statistical region
reports.publisher: INE Chile + Ministerio de Desarrollo Social y Familia
reports.description: Capital region and largest population concentration (~7.4–8.4 million depending on census vs survey frame). Primary domain for ENE, CASEN and many price/activity series. Lower income-poverty incidence than the national average.
reports._notes: Dominant metro node. CASEN 2024: income poverty 13.3% (vs national 17.3%); multidimensional poverty 19.7%. ENE regularly publishes RMS unemployment (recently ~9.6%). Censo 2024 population ~7.4 million in the region.

reports.title: Gran Santiago / continuous urban agglomeration
reports.description: Continuous urban fabric of the capital, spanning multiple communes of the Región Metropolitana. Functional metropolitan area for labour-market and price analysis.
reports._notes: Urban-agglomeration counterpart to the administrative Región Metropolitana. Commune-level census data (Puente Alto, Maipú, Santiago, La Florida, etc.) make the internal structure visible.
_referenced_by: Census geographic products and commune-level population

reports.title: ENE — resultados Región Metropolitana de Santiago
reports.description: Geographic cut of the National Employment Survey for the capital region, including provincial breakdowns inside the RMS.
reports._notes: Practical vehicle for metro labour analysis. Recent moving quarter: RMS unemployment 9.6% (slightly above national). Provincial variation inside the region is reported (Cordillera, Talagante higher; others lower).

reports.title: CASEN — resultados Región Metropolitana de Santiago
reports.publisher: Ministerio de Desarrollo Social y Familia
reports.description: Regional cut of the CASEN survey providing income poverty, multidimensional poverty and living-conditions indicators for the capital region.
reports._notes: Shows the capital region as lower-poverty than the national average under the updated methodology (13.3% income poverty vs 17.3% national in 2024).

reports.title: Producción y exportaciones de cobre / Copper statistics
reports.description: Official and industry statistics of mine copper production (Codelco + private), exports, and contribution to fiscal revenues. Chile remains the world’s largest copper producer (~24% of global output).
reports._notes: Structural backbone of the Chilean economy and external accounts. 2024–2025 production in the 5.3–5.5 Mt range. Codelco ~24–29% of national output; private mining the rest. Copper is the dominant single export and a major fiscal contributor.

reports.title: Codelco — producción y aporte fiscal
reports.description: State copper producer. Statistical identity covering own production, total attributable production, EBITDA, and transfers to the Treasury.
reports._notes: Largest single mining entity. 2025 own production ~1.33 Mt fine copper; consolidated contribution to the fisco reported in the USD 1.7–1.8 bn range. Also entering lithium via joint venture in the Salar de Atacama.

reports.title: Producción de litio / carbonato de litio (Chile)
reports.description: Physical and value statistics of lithium carbonate and related lithium production, concentrated in the Salar de Atacama. Rising component of non-metallic mining and of fiscal revenues (Corfo contracts).
reports._notes: High-growth critical-mineral series. Visible in the IPMin (non-metallic mining) and in fiscal accounts (ingresos por litio de Corfo). Production in the hundreds of thousands of tonnes LCE; joint-venture developments continuing.

reports.title: Comisión Chilena del Cobre (Cochilco) — statistical publications
reports.description: Specialised public agency that compiles and disseminates copper and broader mining statistics, market analysis and production projections.
reports._notes: Authoritative specialised source for copper production, costs, markets and fiscal contribution. Complements the broader INE industrial indices and Central Bank external accounts.

reports.title: Estadísticas de finanzas públicas / Dirección de Presupuestos
reports.publisher: Dirección de Presupuestos (DIPRES) — Ministerio de Hacienda
reports.description: Official public-finance statistics covering central-government revenues (including copper and lithium), expenditure, and fiscal balance. Copper and lithium are explicitly tracked revenue lines.
reports._notes: Public-finance counterpart to the mining production and trade statistics. Copper (Codelco + private mining taxation) and lithium (Corfo) are material and volatile components of fiscal revenue.

reports.title: Censo 2024 — resultados Región Metropolitana
reports.description: Regional and commune-level results of the 2024 Population and Housing Census for the capital region.
reports._notes: Structural demographic baseline for the metro. Commune ranking (Puente Alto, Maipú, Santiago, La Florida, etc.) and ageing indices already published. Feeds survey frames and small-area estimation.

reports.title: Región de Antofagasta — core statistical identity (northern mining)
reports.description: Northern mining region, major copper and lithium production zone. Lower income-poverty incidence than the national average. Strong labour-market participation relative to southern regions.
reports._notes: Mining-specialised region. CASEN 2024 income poverty 16.4% (close to or below national). ENE recent unemployment ~7.2%. Hosts major copper operations and lithium activity in the broader northern corridor.

reports.title: Región de La Araucanía — core statistical identity (highest-poverty contrast)
reports.description: Southern region with the highest income-poverty incidence in the CASEN 2024 results. Tests the statistical hierarchy under higher marginalisation.
reports._notes: Poverty-contrast region. CASEN 2024: income poverty 28.6% (highest among the 16 regions); extreme poverty 13.0%. ENE still produces regular labour-force estimates (recent unemployment ~7.8%). National survey infrastructure reaches the region fully; local independent statistical density is thinner.

reports.title: Región de Valparaíso — core statistical identity
reports.description: Central coastal region, second-largest population after the Metropolitana. Income poverty close to the national average.
reports._notes: Intermediate region. CASEN 2024 income poverty 17.8% (slightly above national 17.3%). Useful bridge between the capital and the extremes.

reports.title: Región del Biobío — core statistical identity
reports.description: South-central region with significant industrial and forestry activity. Income poverty moderately above the national average.
reports._notes: CASEN 2024 income poverty 19.3%. Completes a central–south transect alongside Valparaíso, Maule and Araucanía.

reports.title: CASEN — pobreza por región (income and multidimensional)
reports.publisher: Ministerio de Desarrollo Social y Familia
reports.description: Official regional tabulations of income poverty and multidimensional poverty from the CASEN survey. Primary source for the inter-regional poverty gradient.
reports._notes: Key homogeneity-test product. 2024 ranking (income poverty): Magallanes 9.9%, Metropolitana 13.3%, Antofagasta 16.4%, Valparaíso 17.8%, Biobío 19.3%, Los Ríos 22.3%, Maule 24.3%, Ñuble 23.9%, La Araucanía 28.6%.

reports.title: ENE — resultados Región de Antofagasta
reports.description: Regional cut of the National Employment Survey for the northern mining region.
reports._notes: Recent moving quarter: unemployment ~7.2%, participation relatively high (~65%). Informal employment lower than in southern agricultural regions.

reports.title: ENE — resultados Región de La Araucanía
reports.description: Regional cut of the National Employment Survey for the highest-poverty southern region.
reports._notes: Recent moving quarter: unemployment ~7.8%. Agriculture and public services are important employment absorbers. Demonstrates that the national labour survey reaches the high-poverty region with usable frequency.

reports.title: INACER — Indicador de Actividad Económica Regional (multi-region)
reports.description: Regional economic activity indicators produced for the 16 regions. Geographic counterpart to the national short-term activity measures.
reports._notes: Allows comparison of short-term activity across mining, capital, central and southern regions under a common methodology.

reports.title: Región de Magallanes y de la Antártica Chilena — low-poverty contrast
reports.description: Southernmost region with the lowest income-poverty incidence in CASEN 2024. Completes the geographic poverty gradient.
reports._notes: CASEN 2024 income poverty 9.9% — lowest of the 16 regions. Small population but useful as the opposite pole to La Araucanía.

reports.title: Región del Maule — secondary high-poverty node
reports.description: Central-south agricultural region with elevated income poverty (second-highest after Araucanía in recent CASEN).
reports._notes: CASEN 2024 income poverty 24.3%. Reinforces the central–south poverty gradient alongside Ñuble and La Araucanía.

reports.title: Ley Orgánica Constitucional del Banco Central de Chile (Ley 18.840)
reports.publisher: Poder Legislativo / Banco Central de Chile
reports.description: Constitutional organic law (1989, subsequently amended) that establishes the Central Bank’s autonomy, objectives (currency stability and normal functioning of internal and external payments), governance and powers, including reserve management and monetary-policy instruments.
reports._notes: Foundational static + recurring-citation node for the Chilean central bank — direct analogue of Argentina’s BCRA legal framework and of Mexico’s Banco de México organic law. Continuously cited as the source of the inflation-targeting mandate and of the Bank’s statistical and reserve-management powers.
_referenced_by: Every major BCCh policy and statistical publication
IPoM and financial-stability reports that cite the legal mandate
Academic and legal analyses of central-bank independence in Chile

reports.title: Informe de Política Monetaria (IPoM)
reports.description: Quarterly Monetary Policy Report of the Central Bank. Explains the inflation outlook, the medium-term analytical framework and the implications for the policy interest rate. Statutory reporting obligation to the Senate and the Minister of Finance.
reports._notes: Flagship policy communication product. Published after the March, June, September and December monetary-policy meetings. Central reference for inflation expectations and for the interpretation of the 3% inflation target.

reports.title: Reservas Internacionales del Banco Central de Chile
reports.description: Stock of international reserves managed by the Central Bank under the powers granted by the organic law. Published at high frequency and analysed in the Bank’s financial and external-sector reports.
reports._notes: Key external-vulnerability and monetary-policy indicator. Portfolio composition and investment policy are publicly described; reserves appear in the balance of payments (change in reserve assets) and in the IIP.

reports.title: Marco de metas de inflación (3%) y régimen de tipo de cambio flexible
reports.description: Operational monetary-policy framework: inflation targeting centred on 3% annual CPI inflation, complemented by a flexible exchange-rate regime. Derived from the organic-law mandate to preserve the stability of the currency.
reports._notes: Core policy-framework node. Continuously cited as the reference against which inflation outcomes and policy actions are evaluated. Static institutional commitment with high-frequency operational citation.
_referenced_by: Every IPoM and monetary-policy decision statement
IPC and inflation analysis that refers to the target
Academic and market commentary on Chilean monetary policy

reports.title: Unidad de Fomento (UF) y Unidad Tributaria Mensual (UTM)
reports.publisher: Banco Central de Chile / Servicio de Impuestos Internos
reports.description: Inflation-indexed units of account. The UF is adjusted daily with the IPC and is widely used in contracts, mortgages and financial instruments; the UTM is used for tax and administrative purposes.
reports._notes: Distinctive Chilean institutional feature. The UF links the IPC directly into the financial and contractual system; its daily value is a high-frequency official statistic derived from the consumer-price index.

reports.title: Estadísticas de matrícula del sistema escolar (MINEDUC)
reports.publisher: Ministerio de Educación — Centro de Estudios
reports.description: Official enrolment statistics of the Chilean school system by level, dependency (municipal, SLEP, subsidised private, private), nationality and special-needs status. Annual series.
reports._notes: Core education stock statistic. 2025 school enrolment ~3.54 million. Dependency structure and rising foreign-national share are regularly published. Complements CASEN and census education indicators.

reports.title: Sistema de Medición de la Calidad de la Educación (SIMCE)
reports.publisher: Agencia de Calidad de la Educación
reports.description: National standardised assessment of learning outcomes in language, mathematics and other subjects at key grades (4° and 8° básico, II medio). Annual or near-annual public results.
reports._notes: Flagship learning-outcome indicator. 2025 results show stabilisation/recovery after the post-pandemic drop. Gender gaps and socio-economic gradients are routinely analysed. Continuously cited in education-policy evaluation.

reports.title: Años de escolaridad promedio / educational attainment indicators
reports.publisher: INE / Ministerio de Desarrollo Social y Familia / MINEDUC
reports.description: Average years of schooling of the adult population and related attainment rates, drawn from census, CASEN and administrative sources.
reports._notes: 2024 marked the first time average schooling of the population 18+ exceeded 12 years (the length of compulsory education). Long upward trend documented in CASEN and census series.

reports.title: Fondo Nacional de Salud (FONASA) — coverage and expenditure statistics
reports.description: Public health-insurance fund covering the large majority of the population. Publishes beneficiary counts, benefit expenditure, and modality-of-care statistics (institutional vs free-choice).
reports._notes: Dominant public insurer (~80% of the population in recent survey frames). Benefit expenditure and per-capita spending are key fiscal and health-system indicators. Copago-cero and GES/AUGE programmes are major policy overlays.

reports.title: Encuesta Nacional de Salud (ENS) / National Health Survey
reports.description: Periodic population health survey measuring risk factors, chronic conditions, health-service use and related outcomes. Principal epidemiological input for health policy.
reports._notes: Structural health-status survey. Complements administrative FONASA and hospital statistics with population-based prevalence and risk-factor data.

reports.title: Gasto público en salud (DIPRES functional classification)
reports.description: Public expenditure on health as a share of GDP and in real terms, published in the functional classification of government spending. Includes FONASA, hospital networks and related programmes.
reports._notes: Health spending rose from 2.6% of GDP in 2005 to 5.3% in 2024 — the largest functional increase over the period. Central fiscal counterpart to the FONASA and provider statistics.

reports.title: Gasto público en educación (DIPRES functional classification)
reports.description: Public expenditure on education as a share of GDP and in real terms. Covers school system, higher education and related programmes.
reports._notes: Education spending rose from 3.2% of GDP in 2005 to 4.9% in 2024. Complements the enrolment and SIMCE statistics with the resource side of the education system.

reports.title: Clasificación funcional del gasto público (DIPRES)
reports.description: Official functional breakdown of central-government expenditure (health, education, social protection, etc.) as shares of GDP and in real terms. Used for long-term fiscal sustainability analysis.
reports._notes: Key analytical product for the composition of the state. Health and education have been the fastest-growing major functions over the last two decades; social protection remains the largest single block.

reports.title: Isapres — private health-insurance system statistics
reports.description: Regulatory and statistical reporting on the private health-insurance funds (Isapres): affiliation, premiums, benefits and financial indicators.
reports._notes: Complement to FONASA. Covers the minority but higher-income segment of the dual health-insurance system. Continuously cited in debates on system fragmentation and reform.

reports.title: Ley de Presupuestos / National Budget execution statistics
reports.description: Annual budget law and subsequent execution reports covering revenues (including copper and lithium) and expenditure by ministry and programme.
reports._notes: Operational fiscal framework. Links the copper/lithium revenue lines already captured with the functional spending on health, education and social protection.

dependencies.basis: The Agencia de Calidad de la Educacion's Informe Tecnico de Evaluaciones Nacionales Estandarizadas 2023 states that the establishments and students to be evaluated are identified and validated against MINEDUC's enrolment registry: 'El proceso de empadronamiento telefonico corresponde a la validacion de informacion que se encuentra en la base de datos del Sistema de Informacion General de Estudiantes (SIGE), asi como la del Programa de Integracion Escolar (PIE)', and 'La informacion que entrega la base de datos SIGE y PIE del Ministerio de Educacion' is used to define the establishments in scope. MINEDUC's Centro de Estudios states that its published matricula database is exactly that registry — 'entregada por el Sistema de Informacion General de Estudiantes (SIGE)'.
